title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_area_fade() behaves like geom_area() fills group linear gradient fades fill colour transparent baseline, drawing eye signal rather area underneath.  Use alpha set starting opacity alpha_fade_to control gradient ends. direction can reversed — transparent top, opaque baseline — swapping values.  Multiple groups get gradient:
code: ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy / 1000)) +   geom_area_fade(fill = "#311dfc") +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Unemployed (millions)", title = "US unemployment 1967–2015") ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy / 1000)) +   geom_area_fade(fill = "#d77e7b", alpha = 0.9, alpha_fade_to = 0.05) +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Unemployed (millions)") df <- data.frame(   g = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),   x = c(1, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6),   y = c(2, 5, 1, 3, 6, 7) ) ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = g)) +   geom_area_fade(alpha = 0.85) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c(a = "#f4ae1b", b = "#311dfc"))

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: catenary (Latin catena, chain) curve formed flexible chain cable hanging freely two fixed supports. Contrary widely held belief, parabola — Galileo thought , Leibniz, Huygens, Johann Bernoulli independently derived correct equation 1691: y=acosh(xa)y = \cosh\!\left(\frac{x}{}\right) aa controls steeply chain curves. makes catenary structurally remarkable inverted form: inverted catenary carries weight pure compression bending moments — efficient load path masonry unreinforced concrete. Antoni Gaudí famously designed arches Sagrada Família hanging chains, photographing inverted result, scaling . Gateway Arch St Louis (1965) weighted catenary 192 metres tall. geom_arch() draws inverted catenary curves successive points. shape controlled arch_length (total arc length) arch_height (vertical rise highest endpoint segment). default arc length twice Euclidean distance.
code: df_arch <- data.frame(x = 1:5, y = c(0, 0.3, 0, 0.3, 0))  ggplot(df_arch, aes(x, y)) +   geom_arch(arch_height = 0.6, colour = "#a84dbd") +   geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#a84dbd")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: real-world application Rice House Eltham (1966), whose distinctive roofline consists shallow catenary arched spans rising vertical columns. sketch reconstructs simplified cross-section:
code: rice_house <- data.frame(   x = c(0,   1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 5),   y = c(0,   1,   1,   1,   0) )  ggplot(rice_house, aes(x, y)) +   geom_arch(arch_height = 0.15, linewidth = 2, colour = "#5c4033") +   geom_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = 0), linewidth = 2, colour = "#5c4033") +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#4a7c59", linewidth = 5) +   coord_equal() +   theme_void() +   labs(caption = "Rice House, Eltham (1966) — simplified catenary cross-section")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Chaikin’s corner-cutting algorithm smooths polygonal path iteratively replacing corner two new points placed given ratio along adjacent edges. ratio = 0.25 (default) iterations = 5 path converges smooth B-spline approximation.
code: set.seed(42) dat <- data.frame(x = seq.int(10), y = sample(15:30, 10))  ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +   geom_chaikin(colour = "#311dfc") +   labs(title = "Original path (dashed) vs Chaikin-smoothed (blue)")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: ratio controls aggressively corners cut. ratio = 0.5 new points coincide edge midpoints, producing maximum rounding possible single pass.
code: triangle <- data.frame(x = c(0, 0.5, 1), y = c(0, 1, 0))  ggplot(triangle, aes(x, y)) +   geom_polygon(fill = NA, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.10, mode = "closed", colour = "#f4ae1b") +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.25, mode = "closed", colour = "#d77e7b") +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.50, mode = "closed", colour = "#311dfc") +   coord_equal() +   labs(subtitle = "ratio = 0.10 (yellow), 0.25 (pink), 0.50 (blue)")

what: Smoothing a closed polygon with stat_chaikin
title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: stat_chaikin() can combined geom. Pass geom = "polygon" smooth boundary filled shape:
code: # An irregular hexagon hex <- data.frame(   x = c(0.0, 0.4, 1.0, 1.2, 0.9, 0.1),   y = c(0.2, 1.0, 0.9, 0.3, -0.2, 0.0) )  ggplot(hex, aes(x, y)) +   geom_polygon(fill = "grey85", colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +   stat_chaikin(geom = "polygon", mode = "closed",                fill = "#a84dbd", alpha = 0.45, colour = "#a84dbd") +   coord_equal() +   labs(title = "Original polygon (dashed) with smoothed fill (purple)")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_fourier() fits truncated discrete Fourier transform supplied x/y data renders reconstructed curve. Fewer harmonics produce smoother, low-frequency summary; retaining harmonics reproduces original signal exactly (interpolation artefacts).
code: set.seed(42) n <- 150 df_f <- data.frame(   x = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n),   y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)) +       0.4 * sin(3 * seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)) +       rnorm(n, sd = 0.25) )  ggplot(df_f, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = 1,  colour = "#f4ae1b") +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = 3,  colour = "#d77e7b") +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = 10, colour = "#311dfc") +   labs(     title = "1 harmonic (yellow), 3 (pink), 10 (blue)",     x = NULL, y = NULL   )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: linear drift data dominate low-frequency coefficients, preventing Fourier series capturing periodic structure. Set detrend = "lm" ("loess") subtract trend transform; added back afterwards output remains original scale.
code: set.seed(3) x_d <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 100) df_d <- data.frame(   x = x_d,   y = sin(x_d) + x_d * 0.4 + rnorm(100, sd = 0.2) )  ggplot(df_d, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 0.8) +   geom_fourier(aes(colour = "as is"), n_harmonics = 3,                 linetype = "dashed") +   geom_fourier(aes(colour = "detrend = 'lm'"), n_harmonics = 3, detrend = "lm") +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("as is" = "#a84dbd", "detrend = 'lm'" = "#311dfc")) +   labs(     title   = "With and without detrending",     x = NULL, y = NULL   )

what: Pitfall: irregular spacing with calendar dates
title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Fourier transform (via stats::fft()) assumes observations evenly spaced time. hand calendar dates directly, assumption silently violated: months 28–31 days, consecutive observations distance apart. example maps date — Date vector — x aesthetic asks geom_fourier() reconstruct signal harmonics (n_harmonics = NULL). might expect Fourier curve pass every data point, :  Fourier layer converts dates underlying integer representation (days since 1970-01-01), constructs uniform grid many integer steps, computes inverse FFT grid, draws line interpolated points. grid points fall observation dates, curve misses actual data points even every harmonic included. fix can replace date x-axis plain integer index spacing guaranteed uniform. can restore human-readable year labels scale_x_continuous():  Fourier curve now interpolates data exactly. working irregularly-spaced time series — monthly, weekly, business-day — convert time variable sequential integer index passing geom_fourier() stat_fourier().
code: ggplot(head(economics, 20), aes(date, unemploy)) +   geom_line(linetype = "dotted") +   geom_point(size = 1) +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = NULL, colour = "#311dfc") +   labs(     title = "geom_fourier() with Date x-axis — curve misses observations",     x = NULL, y = "Unemployed (thousands)"   ) eco <- head(economics, 20) eco$tmp <- seq_len(nrow(eco))  # integer positions for year-start labels yr_breaks <- which(format(eco$date, "%m") == "01")  ggplot(eco, aes(tmp, unemploy)) +   geom_line(linetype = "dotted") +   geom_point(size = 1) +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = NULL, colour = "#311dfc") +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = yr_breaks,     labels = format(eco$date[yr_breaks], "%Y")   ) +   labs(     title = "Integer index x-axis — curve passes through every observation",     x = NULL,     y = "Unemployed (thousands)"   )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_lexis() draws 45° lifeline observation start end. required aesthetics x xend; y yend calculated stat_lexis() represent cumulative duration.  gap two events cohort, horizontal dotted segment bridges gap. Set gap_filler = FALSE hide .

title: Introduction to ggpointless

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_lexis() works Date POSIXct objects well numerics. y-axis shows duration native unit scale (days Date, seconds POSIXct).
code: df_dates <- data.frame(   key   = c("A", "B"),   start = c(2019, 2021),   end   = c(2022, 2022) ) df_dates[, c("start", "end")] <- lapply(   df_dates[, c("start", "end")],   function(i) as.Date(paste0(i, "-01-01")) )  ggplot(df_dates, aes(x = start, xend = end, group = key)) +   geom_lexis() +   scale_y_continuous(     breaks = 0:3 * 365.25,     labels = function(i) paste0(floor(i / 365.25), " yr")   ) +   coord_fixed() +   labs(y = "Duration")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_pointless() highlights selected observations — first, last, minimum, maximum, four — points. name reflects particularly useful , conjunction geom_line() friends, adds useful context glance.  Map computed variable location colour distinguish four roles:
code: x   <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = 100) df1 <- data.frame(var1 = x, var2 = rowSums(outer(x, 1:5, function(x, y) sin(x * y))))  p <- ggplot(df1, aes(x = var1, y = var2)) + geom_line()  p + geom_pointless(location = "all", size = 3) loc_cols <- c(   "first"   = "#f4ae1b",   "last"    = "#d77e7b",   "minimum" = "#a84dbd",   "maximum" = "#311dfc" )  p +   geom_pointless(     aes(colour = after_stat(location)),     location = "all",     size     = 3   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = loc_cols) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Locations determined data order, geom_path() — sorted x like geom_line(). matters path crosses :  location = "", points drawn bottom top order: "maximum" < "minimum" < "last" < "first". Passing explicit vector lets override :
code: x       <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi spiral  <- data.frame(var1 = sin(x) * 1:1000, var2 = cos(x) * 1:1000)  p_spi <- ggplot(spiral) +   geom_path() +   coord_equal(xlim = c(-1000, 1000), ylim = c(-1000, 1000)) +   theme(legend.position = "none")  p_spi +   aes(x = var1, y = var2) +   geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)), location = "all", size = 3) +   labs(subtitle = "orientation = 'x'")  p_spi +   aes(y = var1, x = var2) +   geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)), location = "all", size = 3) +   labs(subtitle = "orientation = 'y'") df2 <- data.frame(x = 1:2, y = 1:2) p2  <- ggplot(df2, aes(x, y)) + geom_path() + coord_equal() +        scale_colour_manual(values = loc_cols)  p2 + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),        location = c("first", "last", "minimum", "maximum"), size = 4) +      labs(subtitle = "first on top")  p2 + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),        location = c("maximum", "minimum", "last", "first"), size = 4) +      labs(subtitle = "maximum on top")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_pointless() respects ggplot2’s group structure works naturally facets:
code: ggplot(economics_long, aes(x = date, y = value)) +   geom_line(colour = "grey60") +   geom_pointless(     aes(colour = after_stat(location)),     location = c("minimum", "maximum"),     size     = 2   ) +   stat_pointless(location = "minimum", geom = "text", aes(label = after_stat(y)), vjust = -1) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c(minimum = "#f4ae1b", maximum = "#311dfc")   ) +   facet_wrap(vars(variable), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL)

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: package collection geoms, stats ggplot2. following functions implemented: geom_arch() & stat_arch() – draws catenary arch geom_area_fade() – area plots gradient fill geom_catenary() & stat_catenary() – draws catenary curve geom_chaikin() & stat_chaikin() – applies Chaikin’s corner cutting algorithm geom_fourier() & stat_fourier() – fits Fourier series x/y renders reconstructed curve geom_lexis() & stat_lexis() – draws Lexis diagram geom_point_glow() – adds radial gradient point plots geom_pointless() & stat_pointless() – emphasises observations points See vignette("ggpointless") details examples.

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_area_fade() behaves like geom_area() fills area vertical linear gradient using grid::linearGradient(), fading fill colour top transparent baseline.
code: cols <- c("#f4ae1b", "#d77e7b", "#a84dbd", "#311dfc") theme_set(theme_minimal())  library(ggpointless) df <- data.frame(  g = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),  x = c(1, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6),  y = c(2, 5, 1, 3, 6, 7) )  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = g)) +   geom_area_fade()

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_arch() draws inverted catenary curve (arch) successive points, mirroring geom_catenary() curving upward. shape controlled via arch_length (total arc length) arch_height (vertical rise highest endpoint segment). default arch length twice Euclidean distance.
code: df <- data.frame(x = seq_len(4), y = c(1, 1, 0, 2)) ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +   geom_arch(arch_height = 0.5) +   geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#f4ae1b")

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_catenary() draws flexible curve simulates chain rope hanging loosely successive points. default chain length twice Euclidean distance x/y pair used. shape can controlled via chain_length sag (vertical drop lowest endpoint segment). See vignette("ggpointless") details. Credit : dulnan/catenary-curve
code: ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:5, y = sample(5)),        aes(x, y)) +   geom_catenary() +   geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#f4ae1b")

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_chaikin() applies Chaikin’s corner cutting algorithm turn ragged path polygon smooth one. closed argument controls whether path treated closed polygon. Credit Farbfetzen / corner_cutting.  See also smoothr package.
code: lst <- list(   data = list(     closed_square = data.frame(x = c(0, 0, 1, 1), y = c(2, 3, 3, 2)),     whale = data.frame(x = c(.5, 4, 4, 3.5, 2), y = c(.5, 1, 1.5, .5, 3)),     open_triangle = data.frame(x = c(3, 3, 5), y = c(2, 3, 3)),     closed_triangle = data.frame(x = c(3.5, 5, 5), y = c(0, 0, 1.5))   ),   color = cols,   closed = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE) )  ggplot(mapping = aes(x, y)) +   lapply(lst$data, function(i) {     geom_polygon(data = i, fill = NA, linetype = "12", color = "#777777")   }) +   Map(f = function(data, color, closed) {     geom_chaikin(data = data, color = color, closed = closed)   }, data = lst$data, color = lst$color, closed = lst$closed) +   geom_point(data = data.frame(x = 1.5, y = 1.5)) +   coord_equal()

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_fourier() fits truncated Fourier series (via discrete Fourier transform) supplied x/y data renders reconstructed smooth curve. default harmonics Nyquist limit used, giving exact interpolating fit; reducing n_harmonics progressively smooths result. optional detrend argument ("lm" "loess") removes slow non-periodic trends transform.
code: set.seed(1) n <- 100 df_fourier <- data.frame(   x = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n),   y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) ) ggplot(df_fourier, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +   geom_fourier(n_harmonics = 3, colour = "#311dfc")

title: Additional Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_lexis() combination segment point layer. Given start value end value, draws 45° line indicating duration event. Required aesthetics x xend; y yend calculated automatically.  See also LexisPlotR package.
code: df2 <- data.frame(   key = c("A", "B", "B", "C", "D"),   x = c(0, 1, 6, 5, 6),   xend = c(5, 4, 10, 8, 10) )  ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, xend = xend, color = key)) +   geom_lexis(aes(linetype = after_stat(type)), size = 2) +   coord_equal() +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(df2$x, df2$xend)) +   scale_color_manual(values = cols) +   scale_linetype_identity() +   theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

... but in conjunction with geom_line(), hopefully p <- p + geom_line() p + geom_pointless(location = "all")  p + geom_pointless(location = c("first", "last"))  p + geom_pointless(location = c("minimum", "maximum"))   # The layer computes one additional variable, 'location', # that you can map e.g. to colour p + geom_pointless(   aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = "all",   size = 3 )   # Example with missing first and last observations set.seed(42) df2 <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = c(NA, sample(1:8), NA)) ggplot(df2, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line() +   geom_pointless(location = c("first", "last")) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range #> (`stat_pointless()`). #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`).   # Change the order in which points are drawn when they overlap df3 <- data.frame(x = 1:2, y = 1:2)  p <- ggplot(df3, aes(x = x, y = y)) +   geom_path() +   coord_equal()  # same as location = 'all' p + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("first", "last", "minimum", "maximum") ) +   labs(subtitle = "same as location = 'all'")   # reversed custom order p + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("maximum", "minimum", "last", "first") ) +   labs(subtitle = "custom order")   # same as location = 'all' again p + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("maximum", "minimum", "last", "first", "all") ) +   labs(subtitle = "same as location = 'all' again")   # Use stat_pointless() with a geom other than "point" set.seed(42) df4 <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = sample(1:10)) ggplot(df4, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line() +   stat_pointless(     aes(yintercept = y, colour = after_stat(location)),     location = c("maximum", "minimum"),     geom = "hline"   )   # Example using facets # https://stackoverflow.com/q/29375169 p <- ggplot(economics_long, aes(x = date, y = value)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(vars(variable), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")  p + geom_pointless(   aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("minimum", "maximum"),   size = 2   )

title: ggpointless (development version)
text: New geom_fourier() stat_fourier() fit truncated Fourier series (via FFT) x/y data render reconstructed curve. Supports optional detrending ("lm" "loess") harmonic selection via n_harmonics (#7). New geom_arch() stat_arch() draw inverted catenary curves (arches) successive points, complementing existing geom_catenary() (#4). New geom_area_fade() draws area charts fill colour fades opaque transparent using grid::linearGradient(). fade target alpha controlled via alpha_fade_to (#3). New geom_point_glow() draws points radial gradient glow behind point using grid::radialGradient(). glow colour, alpha, size can customised via glow_colour, glow_alpha, glow_size (#6).
